objective: Continuation authorized by the owner on 2026-10-29 ('Yes, please continue'), taking the recommendation of HUB-SURVIVORS-20261029-001: exact self-similar laws. A hub gadget of a three-bit knot K is an exact counted fixed point when its relation is a placement of K and every allowed leg tuple has the same number of hidden completions; substituting it for every copy then multiplies all counts by that factor per copy and leaves the law unchanged. Questions: (1) which of the 16 classes have such gadgets, at which sizes, with which factors; (2) for the smallest single-scale exact gadgets (all leg pairs at one distance s), the towers they generate: growth, distances, similarity dimension log(copies)/log(s), the law at every scale, and correlations across scales; scoping found parity on the triangle (the Sierpinski gasket, dimension log2 3), twisted not-all-equal on the punctured tetrahedron (dimension 2) and not-all-equal on the punctured Fano plane (dimension log3 7); (3) what local substitution can and cannot build (towers glued through three legs are finitely ramified, never manifolds). Standalone value relative to the nearest known work: exact real-space renormalization on finitely ramified fractals (Gefen, Mandelbrot and Aharony 1980; the Sierpinski gasket and tetrahedron) takes the fractal as given; here the law selects its fractal by exact self-reproduction, uniquely for not-all-equal at its smallest size. Intuitions targeted: space from logic without a drawn space; growth of emergent information (log2 of the factor per copy per level); universally influential cycles; everything relational. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-10-29: exact self-similar laws. An exact counted fixed point rebuilds its knot with the same number of hidden completions on every allowed tuple. Up to six copies these exist exactly for parity (every rebuild, by linearity), twisted not-all-equal (from four copies) and the two three-excluded classes (from five); x or (y != z) is rebuilt but never exact; not-all-equal is exact at seven (Fano). A single-scale exact gadget builds a tower with the same corner law at every level, corners at distance s^k, growth exponent log m / log s, bounded treewidth and three-point cuts (finitely ramified); softening is repelled at least threefold per level. Minimal towers: the Sierpinski gasket (log2 3), the slit triangle (2) and the Fano tower (log3 7). Next: shared-boundary self-reproduction (2/3), deferred to the owner.
stop_rule: Stop when (i) the classes with exact counted fixed points among hub gadgets of at most six copies are classified with their factors and single-scale dimensions; (ii) the towers of the smallest single-scale exact gadgets of parity, twisted not-all-equal and not-all-equal are described by proved structure theorems (growth, distances, dimension, exact law at every scale); (iii) the decision note states what exact self-reproduction can build and what it cannot, with a recommendation. Record negative results.
title: Exact self-similar laws and the towers they build
